_comment: Hand-authored. Beginning play, the key-door pictures and the screen fades, bank 7 $ED1D-$EE14 (the inline far-call arguments are left to the generator). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: Begin play: the entry jingle
regions.description: Entered by JMP from the room and corridor loaders ($EBD1, $EC49, $EC51, $EC89, $ECBB). A = 0 or $80 is the caller's flag: it is stored in slot 0's $0578 and its bit 7 tested at once. With bit 7 set in the labyrinth ($30 bit 6 clear) sound $3C plays (the room-entry jingle; id not looked up); in a corridor, or with A = 0, nothing. RUN: A = $80 in the labyrinth played $3C; A = 0 and A = $80 in a corridor played nothing. The $0578 value stays in the slot until the ship's handler re-initialises it (not checked).

regions.name: Begin play: make the ship, clear the end-of-stage flags
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 1 (the player's ship) with $0788 := $40 (its phase counter; not looked up), $A0 bits 0-1 cleared (end of stage / the player died), $E15F redraws the HUD labels and the AREA/X/Y row, and JMP $D762 selects bank 6 (the object loop's bank) and returns. RUN: $0500 = 1, $0788 = $40, $A0 AND 3 = 0, bank 6 live afterwards.

regions.name: Key doors: arm each exit's hit counter
regions.description: Called when a room loads ($EBC9, $EC26, $EC79). ORs $30 into the four exit bytes $58-$5B (N, W, E, S): the high nibble becomes 3, the number of shots a key-door cover still takes, the low nibble is the key the exit needs (8 = open, no door). RUN: (3, 8, 8, 5) became $33 $38 $38 $35.

regions.name: Key doors: the first key's picture
regions.description: $19:$18 = PPU $1000. Scans the four exits for the first whose key (low nibble) is not 8; if there is none it returns. Otherwise it keeps that key and far-calls bank 2 slot $8006 (-> $8212, the key-icon builder; the 3 inline bytes follow) with A = the key, building its icon in background tiles $00-$03. RUN: exits (3, 8, 8, 5): the builder was called with A = 3 at $1000.

regions.name: Key doors: a second key's picture
regions.description: $19:$18 = PPU $1040. Scans the exits again for the first whose key is neither 8 nor the one just built; if found, far-calls the icon builder with that key (tiles $04-$07). RUN: (3, 8, 8, 5) built key 5 at $1040; (3, 3, 8, 8), (1, 8, 8, 1) and (8, 8, 2, 8) built one icon only; (4, 5, 3, 8) built 4 at $1000 and 5 at $1040 (the third key, 3, gets no picture: at most two keys are drawn per room). CHR: with keys 3 and 5 the tiles at $1000 equalled the icon built for key 3 alone, and at $1040 the icon for key 5 alone. The live CHR of the labyrinth savestate room, which has no key door, holds a generic picture there whose high plane equals the key icons' (they share one high plane), so the ring and bracket the cell notes mention are, as an inference not checked on screen, these tiles: the generic picture when no door needs a key, the key's own picture when one does.

regions.name: Key doors: return
regions.description: The RTS the far call comes back to.

regions.name: Key doors: next exit
regions.description: INY, and the scan loop of the second pass continues until all four exits are done.

regions.name: Fade IN: the screen comes up from black
regions.description: Callers $EC3E, $EC84, $ECAE (after a room or corridor is drawn with the screen off). $EDA1 turns the live palette into the target and blanks the screen colours, $EDE8 switches the display back on, then JMP $EDBD fades. RUN: from black the 24 palette bytes stepped $0F -> $00-hue -> +$10 per step to their saved values in 5 steps, 8 frames, ending with the palette restored, $A3 = $18 (rendering on) and the NMI enabled.

regions.name: Fade set-up: save the palette, black the screen
regions.description: Copies the 24 live palette bytes $0181-$0198 to the fade target $04D0-$04E7 and sets each live byte to $0F (black); $017F = 3 asks the NMI to upload both the background and the sprite palettes. The backdrop $0180 is not touched.

regions.name: Fade IN, entry 2
regions.description: Slot $C0DE. The same set-up, then a wait for the start of vblank ($EDF4) and into the fade loop. The display is NOT switched on by this entry (the caller does that).

regions.name: Fade loop
regions.description: $D950 steps every palette byte one notch toward its target: a byte already equal is left; a byte at $0F jumps to the target's hue at its darkest ($0X); otherwise the brightness (high nibble) goes up $10 if the hue matches and the byte is below the target, and down $10 in every other case (so a different hue fades out first), a borrow giving $0F. $15 counts the bytes that moved and $017F = 3 asks for the upload. When nothing moved the loop returns. With the NMI enabled ($FF bit 7) it waits 2 frames between steps ($FFD1); with the NMI off it does all the steps at once with no waiting. So a colour at brightness 3 takes four steps to black and a fade lasts 8 frames.

regions.name: Fade OUT: the screen goes to black and is switched off
regions.description: Slot $C0ED; many callers ($EC12, $EC65, $F282, $F439, $F65E, $F66B, $F6B8, $FF65). Sets the 24 target bytes $04D0-$04E7 and the backdrop $0180 to $0F, runs the fade loop, then SEI and JMP $D4C7 (rendering off: $A3 = 0 and the PPUMASK bits cleared). RUN: 5 steps at frames 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 ($30 -> $20 -> $10 -> $00 -> $0F for the first colour), returned at frame 8 with all colours $0F, $A3 = 0 and the I flag set.

regions.name: Screen on: sprite 0, the DMC timer, rendering
regions.description: $EDE5 (slot $C060) first sets sprite 0's y from A ($D51E); $EDE8 stores $87 in $05 and in the DMC rate register $4010 (the split timer's starting rate: see the DMC entry), calls $EDF4 and enables interrupts (CLI).

regions.name: Wait for vblank, NMI on, two frames, rendering on
regions.description: Slot $C063. Spins on $2002 until the vblank flag has cleared and then set again (the start of a vblank), then $D4F3 (NMI enable), two frames' wait ($FFD1) and JMP $D4D5 (rendering on: $A3 = $18).

regions.name: Load the attribute patterns
regions.description: Copies the 8 bytes at $EE15 (00 55 AA FF 00 55 AA FF: the whole attribute byte for palette 0, 1, 2, 3, twice) to $0199-$01A0, where the metatile drawer indexes them with the fifth metatile byte AND 7. Called by the corridor priming ($E5BD) and the room loader ($EED0).
